extracted.intended_audience: educated general public, school administrators, parents, and advocates of public physical education
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance and recommendations for establishing and running physical-education (gymnastics) programs in schools and towns, aimed at improving children's and the public's bodily vigor and health. Includes recommendations on facilities, staffing, curriculum integration, attire, and scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical vigor as the foundation of moral and bodily welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical vigor is the basis of all moral and bodily welfare; gymnastics and temperance should go hand in hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument that bodily strength underpins health, moral self-control, and capacity for work; supports prescribing physical exercise broadly as preventive and restorative medicine (cites Asclepiades and historical examples). Use physical culture alongside temperance; avoid doctrines that neglect the body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parents must provide frequent opportunities for active exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: Parents owe their children a provision for a frequent opportunity of active exercise, as they owe them an antiseptic diet in a malarious climate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical obligation on families to enable outdoor play/practice; implication that lack of such opportunities contributes to youth vices and disease. Example: city parents should arrange outlets for children's surplus energy rather than rely solely on mental instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate moral and physical culture in public education
rubrics_metrics.description: On earth, at least, moral and physical culture should be as inseparable as mind and body; our system of public education needs an essential and thorough reform to include gymnastics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical education should be a regular and inseparable part of school curricula rather than an afterthought; treating mind and body separately is presented as a major educational deficiency to be remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every town school should have indoor and outdoor gymnasia
rubrics_metrics.description: Every town school should have an in-door and out-door gymnasium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete facility requirement: schools must provide space and equipment for physical training both indoors (for bad weather) and outdoors; ties into broader recommendation to rebuild education infrastructure to support athletics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint a superintendent of gymnastics for each school district
rubrics_metrics.description: Every school district should appoint a superintendent of gymnastics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/staffing requirement to ensure oversight, curriculum, and quality of physical training across schools; implies professionalization of physical-education leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every town should have a committee of public arenas and devote public space to athletics
rubrics_metrics.description: Every town [should have] a committee of public arenas; cities that can devote tax resources to other causes might well spare an acre of ground for Grecian athletics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civic-level organization and allocation of public land for sport and physical education; recommendation for municipal committees to manage public athletic spaces and events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a yearly field-day festival of competitive gymnastics
rubrics_metrics.description: A field-day, consecrated to Olympic games and the competitive gymnastics of the Turner-hall, should be the grandest yearly festival of a free nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural/political recommendation to celebrate and normalize athletic competition publicly; use festivals and competitions to elevate physical culture and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide domestic substitutes for gymnastic apparatus until schools are equipped
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide, according to our means, some domestic substitutes for the gymnastic apparatus which... the next generation will find in every village hall and every town school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical interim guidance: where formal apparatus is lacking, use homemade or local substitutes so children still get appropriate exercises; encourages creative, low-cost solutions rather than postponing activity until full facilities exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate plenty of time for outdoor exercise in children's schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: We must help our children the best way we can by giving them plenty of time for out-door exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling requirement: schools and parents should ensure children have regular, ample outdoor activity time; opposes cramming children only with intellectual instruction at the expense of physical activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt simple, practical dress for children during exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation dress of the Swedish turners is, in this respect, also the best dress for children — a light jacket, wide trousers and shirts, and broad, low-heeled shoes; in-doors, and in summer-time, shoes and stockings should often be altogether dispensed with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific apparel guidance to facilitate movement and foot development; recommends loosening restrictive clothing during exercise and permitting barefoot activity indoors and in summer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow and encourage barefoot activity for children when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Only men who have their toes perfectly straight will make first-rate runners and wrestlers... this qualification is nowadays a privilege of country lads who are permitted (or obliged) to run around barefoot all summer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates barefoot play/running to develop toes and feet; cites trainer Stephens and rural practice as evidence. Implicit anti-pattern: overprotective footwear and dress that impede natural foot development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design physical culture to equalize development of upper and lower extremities
rubrics_metrics.description: To equalize this difference [between arm- and leg-development] should therefore be the primary object of physical culture, for the harmonious structure of all its parts is an essential condition of a perfectly developed body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program-design principle: select exercises that build arm strength and upper-body development to compensate for daily activities that bias development toward the legs. Example (alluded to): incorporate spear-throwing and upper-body exercises rather than only leg-dominant activities like running.
